'''''Hakea drupacea''''', commonly known as '''sweet-scented hakea''',<ref name="PCA"/> is a tree or shrub which is native to [[South West, Western Australia|south west Western Australia]].

==Description==
''Hakea drupacea'' is an upright rounded shrub growing to  {{convert|1-4|m|ft|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} tall. Smaller branches are hairy. The smooth needle-shaped leaves grow alternately, are {{convert|4-11|cm|in|sigfig=2|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|1-2|mm|in|sigfig=2|abbr=on}} wide ending in a sharp point. The leaf may divide into 2-8 segments. The [[inflorescence]] are short [[racemes]] of sweetly scented white or cream flowers tipped with pink or brownish pollen. The [[pedicel (botany)|pedicel]] is {{convert|4-8|mm|in|sigfig=2|abbr=on}} long and the [[perianth]] {{convert|4-5|mm|in|sigfig=2|abbr=on}} long and smooth. The [[style (botany)|style]] is smooth and {{convert|4-6|mm|in|sigfig=2|abbr=on}} long. The flowers are abundant and appear in the outer leaf axils from March to June. The woody egg-shaped fruit  are {{convert|20-25|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|15-19|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} wide. The fruit surface is smooth with a few black pustules, ending with two prominent horns {{convert|2-4|mm|in|sigfig=2|abbr=on}} long.<ref name="PCA">{{cite book |last1=Young |first1=J A |title=Hakeas of Western Australia:A Field and Identification Guide |publisher=J A Young |isbn=0-9585778-2-X}}</ref><ref name=FloraBase>{{FloraBase|name=''Hakea drupacea'' |id=12227}}</ref><ref name="Holliday"/><ref name="SAF">{{cite web |title=''Hakea drupacea'' |url=http://www.flora.sa.gov.au/efsa/lucid/Hakea/key/Australian%20Hakea%20species/Media/Html/Hakea_drupacea.htm |website=Flora of South Australia:Online |publisher=South Australian Government |access-date=9 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160326043807/http://www.flora.sa.gov.au/efsa/lucid/Hakea/key/Australian%20Hakea%20species/Media/Html/Hakea_drupacea.htm |archive-date=26 March 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="FOAB">{{cite book |editor-last1=Wilson |editor-first1=Annette |last1=Barker |first1=Robyn M. |last2=Haegi |first2=Laurence A. |last3=Barker |first3=William R. |title="Flora of Australia" Volume 17B, Proteaceae 3 Hakea to Dryandra |date=1999 |publisher=ABRS-Department of Environment & Heritage |location=Canberra/Melbourne |isbn=0-643-06454-0}}</ref>

==Taxonomy and naming==
''Hakea drupacea'' was first formally described by [[Karl Friedrich von Gaertner]] in 1807 and given the name ''Conchium drupaceum''. It was also formerly known as ''Hakea suaveolens''.<ref name=APNI>{{APNI | name = ''Hakea drupacea'' (C.F.Gaertn.) Roem. & Schult. | id = 15398}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
Sweet-scented hakea occurs mainly as a coastal species, between [[Albany, Western Australia|Albany]] and east of [[Cape Arid]] and on the [[Recherche Archipelago]] Islands. The species is naturalised in South Africa (where it is known as ''soethakea'', meaning "sweet hakea"), New Zealand and 
coastal [[Victoria, Australia|Victoria]]. Grows in open heath or low shrubland areas with granite hillsides occasionally [[quartzite]] areas or coastal limestone cliffs.<ref name=Holliday>{{cite book|title=Hakeas : a field and garden guide|author=Ivan Holliday|publisher=Reed New Holland |location=Sydney|year=2005|isbn=978-1-877069-14-7}}</ref><ref name="SAF"/><ref name=GRIN>{{cite web | url=http://www.ars-grin.gov/cgi-bin/npgs/html/tax_search.pl|title=Taxon: ''Hakea drupacea'' (C. F. Gaertn.) Roem. & Schult. | access-date=25 September 2011 | work=Germplasm Resources Information Network (GRIN)|publisher=United States Department of Agriculture, Agricultural Research Service, Beltsville Area}}</ref><ref name=vic>[https://vicflora.rbg.vic.gov.au/flora/taxon/83cbec27-e5bf-48c1-a1bd-44cb53e10447 VicFlora ''Hakea drupacea''], Flora of Victoria, Royal Botanic Gardens Foundation Victoria. Retrieved 9 December 2018.</ref>

==Conservation status==

''Hakea drupacea'' is classified as "not threatened" by the Western Australian Government [[Department of Parks and Wildlife (Western Australia)|Department of Parks Wildlife]].<ref name=FloraBase/>
